verse: For godly sorrow produces a repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow produces death. (2 Cor 7:10)
Jesus lifted himself up and said to her, “Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?” She said, “No one, Lord.” And Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go and sin no more.” (Jn 8:10-11)
There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death. (Rom 8:1-2)
Blessed are those whose hearts do not condemn them, and who have not given up their hope. (Sir 14:2)
For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world might be saved through him. (Jn 3:17)
By this we know that we are of the truth and we reassure our hearts before him. For if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and he knows all things. (1 Jn 3:19-20)

Come now, let us reason it out, says the Lord. Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be made white like snow; and though they are red like crimson, they shall become white like wool. (Is 1:18)

He has not dealt with us according to our sins, and he has not repaid us according to our iniquities. For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his steadfast love toward those who fear him. (Ps 103:10-11)
Our steps are made secure by the Lord, when he takes pleasure in our way; though we fall, we will not be cast down, for the Lord holds us by the hand. (Ps 37:23-24)

See what earnestness this godly sorrow has produced in you, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what punishment! In everything you have shown yourselves to be innocent in the matter. (2 Cor 7:11)
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in time of need. (Heb 4:16)
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. (Ps 73:26)
The Lord is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works. The Lord lifts up all who are falling and raises up all who are bowed down. (Ps 145:13-14)

When they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, the man and his wife hid themselves from the Lord God among the trees of the garden. But the Lord God called to the man, and said, “Where are you?” (Gen 3:8-9)
All that the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never cast out. (Jn 6:37)
He will turn back and have mercy on us. He will tread down our iniquities, and he will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea. (Mic 7:19)

But when the goodness and kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not by works of righteousness which we had done, but according to his mercy, by the water of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit. (Tit 3:4-5)

This is a faithful saying and worthy of full acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost. But for that very reason I received mercy, so that in me first Christ Jesus might display all patience, as an example to those who would come to believe in him for eternal life. (1 Tim 1:15-16)
I do not consider that I have already attained it; but this one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what is ahead. (Phil 3:13)
I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. (Phil 3:14)
I am confident of this, that He who began a good work in you will bring it to completion by the day of Jesus Christ. (Phil 1:6)

Do not remember the former things or ponder the things of the past. Behold, I am doing a new thing; now it springs forth—do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. (Is 43:18-19)
If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation, what is old has passed away. Behold, all things have been made new. (2 Cor 5:17)
Let us also lay aside every weight and the sin that surrounds us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus the author and finisher of our faith. (Heb 12:1-2)

He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Therefore, I will most gladly boast in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. (2 Cor 12:9)
I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and distresses for Christ's sake. For when I am weak, then I am strong. (2 Cor 12:10)

Now to him who is able to keep you from falling, and to present you unblemished in the presence of his glory with gladness, to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, dominion, and power, before all time, now and forever. Amen. (Jude 1:24-25)
When as yet we were weak, at the right time, Christ died for the ungodly. For rarely for a righteous man will anyone die, though perhaps for a good man someone would actually dare to die. (Rom 5:6-7)
Therefore, just as through one man’s trespass there came condemnation for all, so also through one man’s act of righteousness there came justification and life for all. (Rom 5:18)

Where sin abounded, grace abounded all the more, so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness leading to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. (Rom 5:20-21)
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God; not from works, so that no one may boast. (Eph 2:8-9)
But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain. (1 Cor 15:10)

The grace of God our Savior has appeared to all men, instructing us to reject impiety and worldly desires, so that we may live soberly and justly and piously in this age, looking forward to the blessed hope and the advent of the glory of the great God and of our Savior Jesus Christ. (Tit 2:11-13)
You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. (2 Tim 2:1)
God proves his love for us in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. (Rom 5:8)
The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost. (Luk 19:10)
Those who are well do not need a physician, but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners. (Mrk 2:17)
The Lord is near to them that are of a broken heart, and he will save the crushed in spirit. (Ps 34:18)
The sacrifice pleasing to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise. (Ps 51:17)

I am the Lord your God, who led you away from the land of the Egyptians, so that you would no longer be their slaves, and who broke the chains around your necks, so that you would walk upright. (Lev 26:13)
I am He who wipes away your iniquities for my own sake. And I will not remember your sins. (Is 43:25)

Who will bring any charge against God’s chosen ones? God is the one who justifies. Who is there to condemn? It is Christ Jesus, who died, rather, was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who indeed intercedes for us. (Rom 8:33-34)

Come to me, all you who labor and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me; for I am meek and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light. (Matt 11:28-30)
Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why are you disquieted within me? Hope in God; for I shall praise him again, my savior and my God. (Ps 42:11)
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our iniquities from us. (Ps 103:12)

I am certain that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor the present things, nor the future things, nor strength, nor the heights, nor the depths, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. (Rom 8:38-39)
I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore with loving kindness have I drawn you. (Jer 31:3)
For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love will not depart from you, neither will the covenant of my peace be removed. (Is 54:10)
The Lord your God is with you; a warrior who gives you victory. The Lord will take delight in you, and in his love he will renew you. (Zeph 3:17)

For a brief moment, I abandoned you, but with great mercies, I will gather you. In a moment of indignation, I have hidden my face from you, but with everlasting love, I will have mercy on you, says your Redeemer, the Lord. (Is 54:7-8)
